properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: md-5 (RustCrypto MD5) is a real shipped dependency: the stun 0.4.4 and turn 0.6.1 crates (libp2p NAT traversal, compiled into the node binary for WebRTC/hole-punching) use MD5 for RFC 5389/5766 long-term credential derivation — MD5(username:realm:password). MD5 is a broken hash (collisions practical), here embedded in an authentication path by a shipped library, not called by this repo's own code. Changeable only upstream (libp2p/stun-rs); presence is what this inventory records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha1 (RustCrypto SHA-1) ships in the tree; its named consumer is webrtc-dtls 0.7.1 (libp2p WebRTC transport), which uses SHA-1 in the DTLS 1.2 handshake (certificate verify/PRF era primitives). SHA-1 is collision-broken (classical, not quantum); the transport itself is the quantum exposure. Changeable only upstream (webrtc-rs); presence recorded.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 ECDSA is the claims pallet's production signature scheme: runtime/common/src/claims.rs:30 imports sp_io::{crypto::secp256k1_ecdsa_recover, hashing::keccak_256} to verify Ethereum-style ECDSA signatures (65-byte r||s||v) over keccak-256 digests when users claim, attest or move pre-sale DOT/KSM; benchmark code at claims.rs:1484 mints keys via libsecp256k1::SecretKey::parse directly. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The RustCrypto ECDSA stack ships: the ecdsa crate (2 versions in the lock) plus k256 0.13.x secp256k1 arithmetic, pulled by substrate's frame-support (git dep, Cargo.lock:3055). This is a second secp256k1-ECDSA implementation available to the runtime build alongside the C-based libsecp256k1 used by the claims pallet. Shor-vulnerable; migrate to ML-DSA when the runtime crypto layer supports it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Poly1305 is the MAC component of the chacha20poly1305 crate tuned on the same line (Cargo.toml:162) — the same logical asset: the Noise transport's AEAD. Tracked via the ChaCha20-Poly1305 entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 is a real signature scheme of this system: ed25519-dalek is release-profile-tuned (Cargo.toml:169), GRANDPA finality session keys are ed25519 (scripts/prepare-test-net.sh:49 generates them with subkey), and the runtime/common sites are #[cfg(test)] helpers for the crowdloan and purchase pallets (dev-seed //verifier / Alice keypairs, signature creation and verify_signature tests). properties.value: BEEFY finality-gadget authority keys are ECDSA on secp256k1 (sp_application_crypto::ecdsa::Public aliased as BeefyId). The two runtime sites are the transform_session_keys helper creating a unique dummy BeefyId when upgrading old session keys (zeroed ECDSA pubkey bytes modified per validator); scripts/prepare-test-net.sh:54 generates real ECDSA-scheme beefy authority keys via subkey. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: x25519-dalek and curve25519-dalek are real, performance-tuned dependencies of the node: X25519 key agreement underpins the libp2p Noise secure-channel handshake used by sc-network for peer-to-peer transport encryption (all validator/P2P traffic is harvest-now-decrypt-later exposed). These profile entries confirm both crates are in the hot build path. Migration: hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768 in the noise/TLS transport of the p2p stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The RustCrypto ed25519 trait crate (2 versions pinned) is the interface layer of the production Ed25519 stack: ed25519-dalek implements it, and sp-core/grandpa use it for GRANDPA finality keys and account signatures. Shor-vulnerable signature scheme; the runtime's ed25519 verification runs inside sp-io/sp-core (external substrate deps) — the crates listed here are what the node binary actually ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: x25519-dalek 1.1.1 (plus a second pinned version) is the X25519 key-agreement implementation for the libp2p Noise transport: libp2p-noise's lock entry (Cargo.lock:4726-4742) lists snow, x25519-dalek 1.1.1, curve25519-dalek 3.2.0 and sha2 directly. Every validator P2P session is key-exchanged with it — harvest-now-decrypt-later. Migrate the transport to hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: curve25519-dalek 3.2.0 (and two more pinned versions) is the Curve25519 arithmetic core beneath x25519-dalek (Noise transport key exchange), ed25519-dalek (GRANDPA/account signatures) and schnorrkel (sr25519 + VRFs). All of these are Shor-vulnerable; the curve is the common root asset for the target's P2P handshake and several signature schemes.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: p256 (RustCrypto NIST P-256/secp256r1 ECDSA + ECDH arithmetic) ships via webrtc-dtls 0.7.1 (libp2p WebRTC/DTLS transport) for DTLS certificate keys and ECDHE. P-256 is fully Shor-vulnerable; migrate the WebRTC transport to a rustls/TLS 1.3 path with hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768 and ML-DSA certs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (pre-standard SHA-3) is genuinely used: production path in the claims pallet hashes Ethereum-style signable messages (claims.rs:546/688), derives the claimant address from the recovered public key (claims.rs:549/680) and mints benchmark keys (1484+); the adder/undying test parachains hash state with keccak256; all four relay runtimes + test-runtime declare tiny-keccak 2.0.2 and import Keccak256 for the claims module. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: aes-gcm 0.10.2 is the AEAD record cipher of webrtc-dtls 0.7.1 (libp2p WebRTC transport, DTLS-SRTP era ciphers including AES-CCM); the second pinned aes-gcm version serves snow/libp2p-noise handshake patterns. AES-GCM is symmetric — quantum impact is only Grover's quadratic speedup against AES-128; not a Shor asset. Recorded as the transport record cipher.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hmac (3 pinned versions, e.g. 0.12.1 via webrtc-dtls, rfc6979 deterministic-ECDSA nonces, pbkdf2) is the MAC/KDF core in the tree. HMAC-SHA2 is quantum-resilient (Grover-only); recorded as symmetric infrastructure feeding DTLS and the ECDSA/BIP32 paths.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2 ships in the tree (pulled via substrate's bip39 mnemonic handling for node key generation / sc-keystore seed derivation, plus the RustCrypto stack). Password-based KDF: quantum-resilient in principle, but iteration counts and salt handling live inside the dependencies — this repo's manifests declare no PBKDF2 parameters, which is the inventory-relevant fact (parameters unobservable here).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: blake2b_simd is a hot-path dependency: BLAKE2b-256 is Substrate's primary hash (state-trie roots, extrinsics, runtime hashing across every runtime in this workspace), which is why the release profile explicitly tunes it. Quantum-resilient (Grover-halved to ~128-bit). Recorded as the target's core hash.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha2 crate (3 pinned versions incl. 0.10.7) — SHA-256/SHA-512 across the build: libp2p-noise's Noise_XX_25519 handshake hash (Cargo.lock:4736), webrtc-dtls, ring internals, substrate hashing primitives. Grover-only quantum impact; confirmed as the hash inventory of the P2P stack.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS 1.3 protocol support comes from the pinned rustls 0.20.8/0.21.6, consumed by libp2p-tls 0.1.0 (TCP TLS transport), quinn-proto 0.9.4 (QUIC transport) and hyper-rustls/reqwest (zombienet-backchannel HTTPS client). TLS 1.3 still key-exchanges with classical ECDHE (X25519/P-256) in these versions — harvest-now-decrypt-later despite the modern protocol. Migration: rustls builds with hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: chacha20poly1305 crate lockfile entry — same logical asset as ALG-3d4cff53: the AEAD record cipher of the libp2p Noise transport via snow. Symmetric, Grover-only quantum impact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: k256 (RustCrypto secp256k1 arithmetic + ECDSA) is pulled by substrate's frame-support (Cargo.lock:3055) — the second secp256k1 implementation shipped to the runtime build alongside the claims pallet's libsecp256k1. Shor-vulnerable; same logical asset family as ALG-6e1f67ab (the ecdsa-crate lockfile entries).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: p256 crate (RustCrypto NIST P-256) shipped via webrtc-dtls 0.7.1 for DTLS certificate keys and ECDHE in the libp2p WebRTC transport. Same logical asset as ALG-a1e29edd (ECDSA P-256 lockfile view); Shor-vulnerable.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: x25519-dalek 1.1.1 (and second pinned version) — the X25519 primitive of the libp2p Noise transport, listed directly in libp2p-noise's lock entry (Cargo.lock:4740) with snow and curve25519-dalek. Same logical asset as ALG-defedad1 (X25519 lockfile entries). Harvest-now-decrypt-later for all P2P sessions; migrate to hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring crypto provider, 2 pinned versions (0.16.20 + 0.17.x): the TLS backend — X25519/P-256 ECDHE, AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 record ciphers, SHA-2, ECDSA/Ed25519 certificate operations — backing rustls (libp2p-tls, QUIC/quinn, hyper-rustls/reqwest), plus direct consumers stun/turn (NAT traversal) and rcgen (cert generation). Neither pinned version has any post-quantum capability; the provider version is what decides when hybrid KEX can be enabled. Changeable here by bumping the lock.
